st: Cook the onions in a dry, wide pot over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring often, until they soften and reduce without browning much.
Add the butter and stir until it melts, then add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] berbere and the tomato paste. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until the mixture darkens and the oil begins to separate.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook 5 more minutes until they break down.
Add the beef, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[2 cups]] water. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low for 60 to 75 minutes, stirring now and then, until the beef is very tender and the sauce is thick.
If the stew gets too dry, add a splash of water. If it is too thin, simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Serve hot on a large round of injera with extra injera on the side for scooping.
Whisk the teff flour and [[3 cups]] water in a large bowl until completely smooth with no lumps. The batter should be thin like heavy cream.
Cover loosely with a cloth and leave at room temperature for at least 10 hours or overnight, until it smells pleasantly sour and shows small bubbles.
After fermenting, pour off any gray liquid on top, then stir the batter and add the salt.
Add up to [[0.5 cup]] more water if the batter seems thick. It should flow easily off a spoon.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Do not add oil.
Pour about a ladle of batter into the pan, swirl to spread it into a thin round, and cover with a lid.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes until the top is covered in tiny holes and set. Do not flip it.
Slide it onto a clean towel to cool. Repeat with the remaining batter, laying the injera out in a single layer so they do not stick.
Cook the onion in a dry pot over medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Add [[3 tbsp]] oil, the garlic and [[1 tbsp]] berbere. Cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until they turn into a thick paste.
Pour in [[2 cups]] water and bring to a gentle simmer.
Put the chickpea flour in a bowl and whisk in [[1 cup]] cold water until smooth.
Slowly pour the flour mixture into the pot while whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Season with [[1 tsp]] salt, turn the heat low, and cook 15 minutes, stirring often, until thick and silky.
Serve hot with injera and add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Rub the chicken with the lemon juice and a little salt, then let it sit while you start the sauce.
Cook the onions in a dry heavy pot over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring, until soft and reduced.
Add the butter, garlic and ginger and cook 2 minutes.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] berbere and the tomato paste. Cook 8 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce is deep red and thick.
Add [[1.5 cups]] water and [[1.5 tsp]] salt and bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken, cover and cook on low for 40 minutes, turning once, until it reaches 165°F (74°C).
Prick each peeled egg lightly with a fork and add to the sauce. Simmer uncovered 10 more minutes.
Serve over injera with the eggs on top.
Pour the fava beans with their liquid into a saucepan and heat gently for 5 minutes.
Mash the beans coarsely with a fork or masher, leaving some texture.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, then cook another 3 minutes.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] olive oil in a small pan, add half of the onion and cook for 2 minutes until just soft.
Spoon the warm beans into a shallow bowl.
Top with the cooked onion, raw tomato, chili and the remaining raw onion.
Drizzle with [[2 tbsp]] olive oil and spoon the yogurt over the center.
Serve with warm bread to scoop.
Mix the flour, water and salt into a stiff dough and knead for 5 minutes. Rest 10 minutes.
Divide the dough into 3 balls and roll each out as thin as you can into a round.
Heat a dry skillet over medium-high heat. Cook each round for 1 to 2 minutes per side until lightly browned and cooked through.
Tear the cooked flatbread into small bite-sized pieces and set aside.
In a wide pan, melt the butter over medium heat and add the garlic and berbere. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the torn bread and toss for 2 minutes until every piece is coated and the edges crisp.
Pile the bread on a plate and spoon the yogurt over or alongside.
Rinse the lentils and fava beans and soak in cold water for 30 minutes.
Drain, then place in a pot with [[3 cups]] fresh water and bring to a boil.
Simmer 30 minutes until both are completely soft, skimming any foam.
Drain, keeping a little of the cooking water.
Blend the legumes with the garlic, chili, lemon juice, olive oil and [[1 tsp]] salt, adding the cooking water a spoon at a time.
Whip until the dip is smooth and fluffy, adding a splash of water if it is too thick.
Taste, adjust lemon and salt, and serve with flatbread or injera.
